Projective-space example uses constant rank-one line bundles. BG diagonal is an Isom morphism represented by finite etale schemes. Elliptic example asserts Neron existence without unqualified uniqueness. Fell character tests and finite sums both are nonnegative scalar multiples. Affine quotients use explicit finitely generated invariants. Finite imprimitivity fibres and ax+b inducing characters are finite-dimensional and separable.

Reviewed root-coordinate, Levi, simple-reflection, Bruhat, parabolic and GLn uses. Every double-coset use binds B containing T; all simple-root systems are tied to that B. The standard Levi is called with the corresponding base, and G/P is integral here because split reductive G is geometrically integral, so completeness is well typed even for nonsmooth P. No root or coroot claim is attributed to the lattice-only interface.

Reviewed Alexander consumers: each uses gcd E0, unit ambiguity or the unchanged total-linking polynomial normalization; none relies on the removed nonprincipal-ideal caveat. Fox and Burau formulas distinguish multivariable specialization from the absolute one-variable polynomial. Unknot has its required explicit circle mark. Position-momentum induction uses C as fibre and separable L2(Rn). Rouquier example uses the unchanged internally shifted generator complexes, not the corrected source-comparison sentence. Five-strand kernel argument uses explicit twist actions, rather than the erroneous bigon-complement-component formulation.

Reviewed projective quotient and algebraic-space consumers: reductive G is present throughout invariant-section arguments, and affine chart maps are induced by inclusions of complex algebras. Local good restrictions in the locality lemma are C-morphisms and force that global property. The kernel-pair and etale-relation statements use representability of diagonals as morphisms and scheme-valued equality loci, never the corrected object assertion.

Reviewed arithmetic consumers: parameter DVR translations are only used on their rational domains, spreading the translation and inverse together. Picard positive charts are used on the abelian variety with supplied rational unit, where the rigidified sheaf has actual line-bundle representatives. Cartier duality is used only for finite affine commutative group schemes, including the finite mu_n-torsor F constructed in theta splitting. Group-component restrictions and multiplication use correctly typed group laws, kernels and base changes. No consumer item edit is mathematically necessary in this pass.
